samples.summary: `@`-suffix stripping re-opens the exact path forgery the new match is meant to close
samples.evidence:
`ciRunsFor` accepts any run whose `path`, TRUNCATED AT THE FIRST `@`, equals `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

    String(r?.path ?? "").split("@")[0] === CI_WORKFLOW_PATH

The justification for path-matching (checks.mjs:54-56, and docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1902-1910) is that "only one file can occupy it, so a run's path names the file that produced it". The `@` tolerance breaks that uniqueness: `@` is a legal character in a git path, and GitHub Actions picks up ANY `.github/workflows/*.yml`, so a file committed at `.github/workflows/ci.yml@pwn.yml` produces runs whose reported path truncates to exactly `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and is therefore accepted as the real CI workflow.

Attack chain, against the very actor the new comment names (an `agent:managed` human PR — agent-review-panel.yml:51 states such a PR *can* push `.github/workflows/**`): in one PR, delete/rename the real `ci.yml` (otherwise the new all-runs-green rule would still require the real run) and add `.github/workflows/ci.yml@pwn.yml` containing `name: CI`, `on: pull_request`, and a single `run: true` job. The forged file's `name: CI` also satisfies the panel's name-matched `workflow_run` trigger (agent-review-panel.yml:27-28), so the panel runs; `ciConclusion` then sees exactly one 'CI' run, green, and gate 1 — the gate that is documented to mean "the tests passed" — is satisfied with zero tests executed. The PR is flipped to ready and the hand-off comment asserts "✅ CI verification … is green" to the human reviewer. Merge still needs branch-protection approval (and CODEOWNERS covers `/.github/workflows/`), which bounds this to a false assurance rather than a merge, but it defeats the new control on its own terms. A strict `r.path === CI_WORKFLOW_PATH || r.path.startsWith(CI_WORKFLOW_PATH + "@")` is no safer for the same reason; the called-workflow case would need the ref suffix validated (e.g. `@refs/…`/`@<40-hex>`) or the run matched by `workflow_id` instead of a string path.

samples.summary: Gate 1 is still forgeable by editing ci.yml itself, so the strengthened "unforgeable" claim does not hold against the attacker it names
samples.evidence: The new doc block (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1902-1912) and the CI_WORKFLOW_PATH comment justify path-matching by the threat "anyone able to push a branch to the base repo could add .github/workflows/anything.yml with name: CI", and explicitly note that an `agent:managed` human PR is on the same promote path and is NOT restricted from pushing workflow files. Matching on path does not address that attacker at all: for a `pull_request` event GitHub executes the workflow files from the PR's own tree, so the same actor can simply edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in the PR to drop or neuter its jobs. The run still comes from the real path, still concludes `success`, `ciConclusion()` (checks.mjs:84) returns "success", and gate 1 passes with no tests run — after which mark-ready.mjs:248 posts a hand-off comment telling the human reviewer that "CI verification (`verify:self` and `verify:integration`) is green". Nothing in the promote path (agent-review-panel.yml:1444-1503) rejects a PR that modifies `.github/workflows/**`, and mark-ready never checks that the run's workflow file matches the base branch's version. CODEOWNERS (.github/CODEOWNERS:53) requires maintainer review of `/.github/workflows/` before MERGE, which caps the damage, but the promotion gate itself and its 'unforgeable' documentation over-claim. Hardening: refuse promotion when the head diff touches `.github/workflows/**`, or verify the CI run's `head_sha` workflow content against the base ref.

samples.summary: The panel/fix triggers still identify CI by display NAME, so the forged-'CI' run the delta defends mark-ready against still drives agent jobs that push commits
samples.evidence: The delta hardens the READ side (mark-ready/set-state now match `.github/workflows/ci.yml` by path) but leaves every TRIGGER side name-based: `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:27-28` (`workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"]`) and `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:20-21` (same). The `ci` job then polls only the triggering run id and exports its conclusion (lines 267-328), which is what `if:` gates the `fix` job at line 1627 — the arm that runs the agent and PUSHES a commit to the PR branch. A second workflow file with `name: CI` (the exact forgery CI_WORKFLOW_PATH's comment describes) therefore still: (a) starts the review panel with an attacker-chosen conclusion, and (b) by concluding `failure`, drives agent-iterate-ci's pushing arm — bypassing the 'CI conclusion is a MUTEX between the two pushing arms' invariant documented in checks.mjs:112-119, and doing so even while the real CI run is red or still in flight. Promotion itself remains gated by mark-ready's path check, so this is agent-invocation/mutex abuse rather than a promotion bypass; I could not fully confirm GitHub's matching behaviour when two workflow files share a `name:`. Fix: add `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to the `gate`/`ci` job `if:` in both workflows.

samples.summary: `ciConclusion` accepts any run of the CI file regardless of trigger event or actor
samples.evidence: `ciRunsFor`/`ciConclusion` filter on `path` only — not on `event`, `actor`, or `head_repository`. Any future trigger added to `ci.yml` that can be started by a low-privilege actor for a PR head SHA (`workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch`, a `pull_request_target`-style variant) would produce a run that counts as gate-1 evidence, potentially one whose inputs the caller chose. Today `ci.yml:6-28` only has `push:[main]`, `pull_request:[main]` and `merge_group`, so this is latent rather than live, and the new all-runs-green rule is fail-closed for extra RED runs; the exposure is only for extra GREEN runs when the real `pull_request` run is absent. Constraining to `event in {pull_request, merge_group, push}` would make the evidence's provenance explicit alongside the new path constraint.

verdict.reason: The line exists as quoted (checks.mjs:62), but the claimed weakening does not: the `@`-truncation grants no capability that strict equality withholds. The attack requires an actor who can commit under `.github/workflows/**` AND must neutralise the real `ci.yml` (the reviewer concedes this, because ciConclusion at checks.mjs:84-89 requires every matched run green). That same actor can simply gut `ci.yml` in place: CI is `pull_request`-triggered off the branch's own tree (ci.yml:6-10, no paths filter), a fact this repo itself documents at agent-review-panel.yml:46-52 ("a push/pull_request trigger would run the branch's own copy of this file"). A gutted-in-place ci.yml keeps `name: CI` (ci.yml:4), so it fires the panel's name-matched trigger (agent-review-panel.yml:27-28) and reports `path` exactly `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — matching under strict equality, startsWith, a validated `@refs/...` suffix, or `workflow_id` (ids survive content edits). Identical outcome, identical prerequisite, and every fix the finding proposes leaves it intact. Gate 1's unforgeability rests on the agent App lacking the `workflows` scope (agent-review-panel.yml:50-51), not on path-string uniqueness, so this line neither introduces nor re-opens the bypass; the truncation serves the documented called-workflow case (checks.mjs:60, checks.test.mjs:466-468). Impact is also bounded by CODEOWNERS on /.github/workflows/ (.github/CODEOWNERS:30,53) plus branch protection. Not a blocking security defect at this location.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the repository. checks.mjs:41-58 carries the docblock naming the exact attacker ("anyone able to push a branch to the base repo"; "an `agent:managed` human PR is on the same promote path and is not restricted") and mitigates only the second-workflow-file variant via path matching (checks.mjs:62). ci.yml:6-10 triggers on `pull_request`, so a same-repo PR's own edited `ci.yml` is what executes; gutting its jobs still yields a concluded-`success` run recorded at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which ciConclusion (checks.mjs:84-89) reports as "success" and mark-ready.mjs:125-139 accepts as gate 1 with no tests actually run. This is a weakened/over-claimed enforcement gate, squarely in the security lens (authorization / evidence forgery), and the mitigation gap is real rather than hypothetical.

mergedFrom.summary: Gate 1 identifies its "unforgeable" CI evidence by the workflow's mutable DISPLAY NAME rather than by workflow path/id — the exact surface the doc in this delta names as the forgery vector

finding.summary: Gate 1's "unforgeable" CI evidence is matched by workflow DISPLAY NAME, not workflow path/id — a branch-added workflow named `CI` forges it, and this change pins the name filter as the invariant
finding.evidence: `ciPassed` selects evidence with `(data.workflow_runs ?? []).filter((r) => r.name === "CI")` and then takes the newest by `created_at` (mark-ready.mjs:133-137). `name` is the run's display name, which is whatever the workflow file's `name:` key says — it is not tied to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Anyone who can push a branch to the BASE repo can add `.github/workflows/anything.yml` with `name: CI` on `push`; its run is recorded against the same `head_sha`, is newer than the real CI run, and `runs[0].conclusion === "success"` returns true even when the genuine CI run for that SHA failed. That path is not hypothetical for this repo: the panel's own header notes "The agent App cannot push `.github/workflows/**`, but an `agent:managed` human PR can" (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:51), and `agent:managed` is an opt-in label (line 190) that puts such a PR on the promote path. The new test added here (`scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:184-209`) elevates this name filter to a pinned security property while only exercising differently-NAMED runs, so it documents the check as sound rather than exposing the same-name forge. `set-state.mjs:226` filters CI the same way. A robust filter would key on `r.path === ".github/workflows/ci.yml"` (or `workflow_id`), which cannot be spoofed by a second file.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in the working tree. mark-ready.mjs:136 calls `ciConclusion(data.workflow_runs)`, and checks.mjs:61-63 filters CI runs by workflow PATH (`String(r?.path ?? "").split("@")[0] === CI_WORKFLOW_PATH`, checks.mjs:58 = ".github/workflows/ci.yml"), not by display `name`. checks.mjs:84-89 further requires EVERY CI run for the SHA to be success and returns null on any unfinished run, so the claimed `created_at` "newest wins" sort is also absent. set-state.mjs:228 uses the same `ciConclusion(runs)` helper, not the claimed `r.name === "CI"` filter at line 226. The exact forge vector the finding says is unexercised is directly tested: mark-ready.test.mjs:218-229 ("gate 1 is not forgeable by a SECOND workflow file that calls itself 'CI'") with `{name:"CI", path:".github/workflows/pwn.yml", conclusion:"success"}` as the newest run, and checks.test.mjs:443 asserts the same. The quoted `r.name === "CI"` lines exist only under `.trusted/`, which is a transient checkout of `main` staged and deleted by the review workflows (agent-review-panel.yml:520-528) — i.e. the pre-change baseline this branch replaced, not repository source. The reviewer's own recommended fix (key on `r.path`) is verbatim what the code already implements.
